newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sacks general Kobets after graft charges.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sacks general Kobets after graft charges.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin has sacked General Konstantin Kobets, a once loyal ally accused of corruption, from his top military posts, the Kremlin announced on Tuesday.

Military prosecutors have brought charges of bribe-taking, embezzlement and illegal possession of arms against Kobets, who played a vital role in backing Yeltsin during a hardline coup attempt in 1991 and a revolt in 1993.
Kobets, 57, has denied all charges against him.
Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky told reporters that Yeltsin, who is commander-in-chief of the Russian armed forces, had reacted "with indignation" to reports about the charges against Kobets.
He sacked Kobets from the posts of chief military inspector and a deputy defence minister and dismissed him from the military service.
In 1991, Kobets was in charge of defending the White House parliament building from which Yeltsin led resistance to a hardline coup against then Soviet president Mikhail Gorbachev.

Two years later when the top brass were reluctant to use force to decide a bloody power-struggle between Yeltsin and the conservative parliament, Kobets helped the president persuade a small group of troops to intervene and crush the opposition.
Kobets, whom Yeltsin made defence minister in 1991 for a brief period, was in hospital.
Yeltsin and his new reformist government launched an anti-corruption drive last week, promising to cleanse the state of dishonest officials.

Chief Military Prosecutor Yuri Dyomin told Izvestia newspaper last Friday that 20 generals and admirals and 100 colonels were under investigation -- a situation made all the more scandalous by the sorry state of the lower ranks, who were going hungry, deserting and committing suicide in unprecedented numbers.
